title: Trace
description:
Project Type: Single-POV Procedural Mystery (Standalone)
Tone: Restrained, observational, forensic — closer to Tana French than Agatha Christie


Story Premise:


Detective Inspector Esra Doyle is the only woman on the Major Investigations team in Cromer, a fading English port town. When a fisherman finds a severed thumb in a lobster pot, Esra discovers it belongs to a missing teenage girl who was last seen leaving an end-of-pier funfair three weeks earlier. As Esra follows the trail, she uncovers a network of disappearances tracing back to an unlicensed forensics lab operating out of a decommissioned coastguard station — a lab whose existence implicates the same Senior Investigating Officer who passed her over for promotion last spring.


Key Characters:


- Esra Doyle (POV): late 30s, divorced, recovering alcoholic, two years out of frontline work after a sectioning incident. Sees patterns where others see chaos; struggles to articulate hunches in formal reports.
- DCI Mark Penhaligon: her superior. Bluff, fatherly, dangerous.
- Dr Iolanthe "Iola" Pryce: a forensic pathologist with a private practice on the side. Esra's only ally inside the system.
- The girls: Five missing teenagers, four unsolved, one returned mute.


Project Goals:


- Test restraint: the pipeline should produce a procedural without cliché thriller pyrotechnics
- Stress-test foreshadowing and payoff mapping with a layered clue structure
- Validate that single-POV deep interiority works at chapter scale
- Audit the voice profile for first-person procedural register (clipped sentences, sensory undertow, dry humour)
